# Reduce native proving time and retained memory

Native proving retains full working arrays, allocates oversized lookup intermediates and repeats sparse commitment and opening work. This change bounds temporary tables and batches, reclaims consumed buffers, shares immutable hints, encodes lookup indices more tightly and constructs sparse commitment rows with less work.

**Topic** native prover time and memory. **Type** Performance and ownership changes. **PR target** `main`. **Prerequisite** [#373](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/373).

The branch records the merged main history with an identical source tree to tested head `6d3e3a24daf3a120baa05711e8ebac28d801daa9`. Its prerequisite changes remain part of the comparison with main until merged.

**Primary source PRs** [#343, shared commitments](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/343), [#337](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/337), [#345](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/345), [#346](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/346), [#347](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/347), [#348](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/348), [#349](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/349), [#350](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/350), [#351](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/351), [#352](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/352), [#353](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/353), [#354](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/354), [#356](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/356), [#357](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/357), [#358](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/358), [#360](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/360), [#362](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/362), [#363](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/363), [#365](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/365).

## Review order

1. Shared range commitments from part A of #343.
2. Bound lookup and range table construction.
3. Parallel sumcheck and commitment scheduling.
4. Sparse rows and active opening prefixes.
5. Buffer reclamation and shared ownership.
6. Compact and fully populated index storage.

## Existing evidence

These are recorded comparisons for individual changes. Each has its own control and workload; performance of the combined branch is unmeasured. The original PRs retain source revisions, hardware, flags and artifact links.

| Scope | Recorded control | Recorded candidate | Change | Meaning and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Complete policy, commitments plus proving | 31.08 min | 22.04 min | 9.04 min lower (29.1%) | #360; 29.1% lower, one complete sample each; process peak does not improve |
| Complete policy peak RSS | 200.97 GiB | 163.26 GiB | 37.71 GiB lower (18.8%) | #363 optional-index comparison; 18.8% lower, with 1.04% more commitments/proving time |
| Complete action peak RSS, fully populated indices | 140.26 GiB | 125.08 GiB | 15.18 GiB lower (10.82%) | #363 latest representation; 10.82% lower, with commitments/proving increasing from 1,710.55 to 1,721.48 s; one sample each |
| Complete action, witness construction plus commitments | 846.42 s | 667.44 s | 178.98 s lower (21.15%) | #337 latest update; 21.15% lower, one sample each |
| Uniform / missing synthetic rows, warm time | 157.48 / 132.91 ms | 165.08 / 146.41 ms | 7.60 / 13.50 ms higher (4.82% / 10.16%) | #337 regressions of 4.82% / 10.16%; retain these controls |
| Combined #356–#358 policy, commitments and proving | 29.75 min | 30.72 min | About 0.97 min higher (3.3%) | One sample per variant; does not isolate the three changes |
| Same combined policy, peak RSS | 213.48 GiB | 213.18 GiB | 0.30 GiB lower (0.14%) | Small observed change, without a repeatability claim |

## Implementation and review examples

Commitment reuse from #343 is included here. Checked target-group transport is in the separate verifier/decoding change.

The latest #337 generator-sum cache and #363 fully populated index representations are included. Ownership changes preserve the committed polynomials and transcript order. The #357 regression imports the evaluation trait explicitly so the default tests compile.

The combined model experiment for #356–#358 did not show an overall speed gain. These changes retain their independently tested allocation/copy effects and remain separate commits for review. No cumulative complete model speedup is claimed for this branch.

## Measurement conditions

- Lookup preparation, #360. The complete policy comparison uses one sequential accepted sample per source on the same Xeon Platinum 8272L with 48 workers. Both retain the original registration and required consumers and rejection checks. Whole-command peak RSS rises from 212.83 to 213.44 GiB, so this is a proving-time gain without a complete-process memory reduction. [Pinned comparison](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/blob/cc299bc/native-atlas/evidence/2026-09-18-policy-lookup-bounded/results.md).
- Fully populated indices, #363. One sequential action sample per source on the same Xeon E7-8890 v4, 32 native workers and 16 consumer workers, with matching model, registered setup and tracing. Only `compact_indices.rs` changes in the integrated Rust source. [Pinned source and complete receipt comparison](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/tree/9d884f21d547e19ee15fbd67642d9ac85904aa57/native-atlas/evidence/2026-09-20-action-present-indices).
- Combined evaluation and ownership changes, #356–#358. One sample per configuration on Xeon Platinum 8272L with 48 workers. The whole native command rises from 2,971.14 to 3,065.34 seconds (94.20 seconds or 3.17% higher). This comparison establishes neither an overall improvement nor a repeatable regression and cannot isolate any constituent change. [Pinned complete comparison](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/blob/cc299bc/native-atlas/evidence/2026-09-18-policy-evaluation-combined/results.md).
- RSS denotes memory resident in the process. The allocation counts in the original reports measure particular arrays and are not whole-process peaks. These single complete samples do not establish repeatability.

## Validation

Linux validation at `6d3e3a24daf3a120baa05711e8ebac28d801daa9`, Rust 1.95.0, strict warnings, eight Rayon workers and the repository test profile:

- Formatting passes. Native library tests pass 188 ordinary cases and 331 ZK cases.
- Strict Clippy passes for all native library, test and example targets with ZK, and for the whole workspace with and without ZK.
- Differential controls compare sparse commitments, bounded lookup preparation, compact index representations, owned and borrowed openings, complete arithmetic messages and original tensor openings. Malformed commitments, evaluations and hidden producers remain rejected.

Integration repairs reconcile the owned opening API, compact-index test arguments and hidden claim identities in preparation fixtures. The missing evaluation-trait import and a redundant test cast are repaired separately. No new complete-model performance comparison is claimed for the assembled branch.

## Experimental ONNX scope

The foundation's separate ONNX ZK test run reports 127 passes, 26 failures and 29 ignored tests. That parent result is preserved in the validation record. This branch validates the native API and does not claim completion of the experimental ONNX dispatcher or a green complete-workspace ZK test job. No test or proof predicate is relaxed.

# Reduce native verification and checked decoding cost

Native verification repeatedly combines group elements, searches opening lists, performs expensive checked decoding in the pairing target group (GT), and retains temporary witness data. This change adds group multiscalar multiplication (MSM), indexed opening membership, checked compact encoding and shorter subgroup checks, and releases data after its last use. Transcript order and rejection behavior are preserved.

**Topic** native verifier and transport. **Type** Performance and new transport with equivalent validation predicates. **PR target** `main`. **Prerequisite** [#374](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/374).

The branch records the merged main history with an identical source tree to tested head `2e415e2a8bfd71678b7b62766a149b259dc166ce`. Its prerequisite changes remain part of the comparison with main until merged.

**Primary source PRs** [#343](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/343), [#344](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/344), [#355](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/355), [#359](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/359), [#361](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/361), [#364](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/364), [#368](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas/pull/368).

## Review order

1. Checked compact GT transport from part B of #343.
2. Parallel combinations and target group MSM.
3. Ordered opening membership and deduplication.
4. Exact subgroup and cyclotomic checks.
5. Consume verifier stages and intermediate rows after their last use.

## Existing evidence

These are recorded comparisons for individual changes. Each has its own control and workload; performance of the combined branch is unmeasured. The original PRs retain source revisions, hardware, flags and artifact links.

| Scope | Recorded control | Recorded candidate | Change | Meaning and limits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Complete action validation including internal rejection controls | 101.053578 s | 59.088359 s | 41.965219 s lower (41.53%) | #359; 41.53% lower, two samples per variant, same saved proof |
| Complete action validation including controls | 57.176931 s | 54.375884 s | 2.801047 s lower (4.90%) | #364; 4.90% lower, four samples per variant; distinct control from #359 |
| Native transport plus external application codec | 23,377,721 bytes | 9,663,363 bytes | 13,714,358 fewer bytes (58.66%) | #343 integration result; the generic compact GT wrapper alone does not own this saving |
| Complete saved receipt, mean process maximum RSS | 1.4848 GiB | 0.9876 GiB | 0.4972 GiB lower (33.49%) | #368; two observations per variant, distinct complete-verifier control |

## Implementation and review examples

The opening index preserves insertion and transcript order while replacing repeated linear membership searches. Group MSM and parallel combinations retain the same group result. Compact GT decoding checks canonical fields and exact subgroup membership. Faster cyclotomic powering is used only after the required membership predicates succeed.

The storage change consumes completed stages and intermediate sparse rows, moves builder inputs, and removes witness-only retained copies from a distinct verifier wrapper. An independent oracle retains the original matrix construction. Matrix entries, variable order, aliases, commitments and transcript order stay identical.

Verification measurements use the same saved proof. Decode time, honest verification and validation including deliberate rejection trials are distinct scopes. The transport size in the table also includes an external codec, so the generic GT wrapper alone does not own that saving.

## Measurement conditions

- Opening membership, #359. The control already includes the target group MSM from #355. Two samples per variant use the identical saved proof and keys, Xeon E7-8890 v4 and 32 workers in control/candidate/candidate/control order. Production builds disable debug assertions. Timing includes internal rejection trials. Profiling is separate.
- Checked cyclotomic powering, #364. The control is #361's ordinary powering, remeasured in this experiment. Four samples per variant use the same saved proof, host and 32 workers in two control/candidate/candidate/control blocks. The two verifier percentages in the table have different controls and cannot be multiplied.

- Verifier storage, #368. Linux Xeon E5-2640 v4, 20 exposed logical CPUs, eight Rayon workers, Rust 1.97.1 release build with `host`. Two observations per variant in ABBA order use independently built targets and the same complete saved receipt. The application control includes registered parameters, membership certificates, batched decoding, transcript reversal and allocator reuse; only the storage patch differs. Mean whole-command time is 61.195 versus 60.455 seconds (0.740 seconds or 1.21% lower). This is a host-memory observation, without a guest-capacity or proving claim. Measured source is `4c60effc0e22a8f165845364062eab37f4f7f02f`; final original head changes only test slice borrowing. [Exact source maps, timings and reproduction](https://github.com/ICME-Lab/zkARc/blob/4205b03c1729e079b95e1c998d478ddc5482ecbe/native-atlas/blindfold-verifier-storage/results.md).

## Validation

Linux validation at `2e415e2a8bfd71678b7b62766a149b259dc166ce`, Rust 1.95.0, strict warnings, eight Rayon workers and the repository test profile:

- Formatting passes. Native library tests pass 203 ordinary cases and 353 ZK cases.
- Strict Clippy passes for all native library, test and example targets with ZK, and for the whole workspace with and without ZK.
- Controls cover ordered opening membership, missing and duplicate openings, noncanonical fields, zero and non-subgroup points, and the exact cyclotomic predicate. The independent storage oracle compares complete matrices, layouts, aliases and repeated-opening constraints with the original construction.

The three storage differential tests from #368 are included. No new complete-model performance comparison is claimed for the assembled branch.

## Experimental ONNX scope

The foundation's separate ONNX ZK test run reports 127 passes, 26 failures and 29 ignored tests. That parent result is preserved in the validation record. This branch validates the native API and does not claim completion of the experimental ONNX dispatcher or a green complete-workspace ZK test job. No test or proof predicate is relaxed.
